anchors.paper_title: Eeg Motor Imagery Dataset From The Phd Thesis "Commande Robuste D'Un Effecteur Par Une Interface Cerveau Machine Eeg Asynchrone"
anchors.paper_venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
anchors.reason: The Zenodo record describes the same data: 8 subjects, 16 electrodes, 512Hz, g.tec g.USBamp, right hand/feet/rest, 3 s trials. It matches the dataset's DOI 10.5281/zenodo.806022.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 16 active electrodes with a g.tec g.USBamp amplifier, referenced to the earlobe, in standard office conditions. Subjects imagined right hand movement, foot movement, or rest following visual cues lasting 3 seconds, with 20 trials per class and no feedback. Acquisition used Matlab/Simulink with g.tec drivers.

citation_details.title: A Novel Missense Mutation in the TGF-β-binding Protein-Like Domain 3 of FBN1 Causes Weill–Marchesani Syndrome with Intellectual Disability
citation_details.author: Mahdieh Hassani, Sara Taghizadeh, Anahita Farahzad, Mahvash Habibi, Setareh Banitalebi, Mahbubeh Kasiri, Alireza Sadeghi, Ahoura Nozari
citation_details.abstract: Background: Weill–Marchesani syndrome (WMS) is a rare connective tissue disorder characterized by locus heterogeneity and variable expressivity. Patients suffering from WMS are described by short stature, brachydactyly, joint stiffness, congenital heart defects, and eye abnormalities. This disorder is inherited in two different modes; the autosomal dominant form of the disease occurs due to a mutation in FBN1 , and the recessive form results from mutations in ADAMTS10 , ADAMTS17 , or LTP2 genes. Materials and Methods: The family recruited in this study was a consanguineous Iranian family with an intellectually disabled girl referred to the Sadra Genetics laboratory, Shahrekord, Iran. The clinical history of family members was investigated. Whole-Exome Sequencing (WES) for the proband was performed. Sanger sequencing was used to assess the segregation of candidate variants in the other family members. Results: Whole-exome sequencing analysis revealed a novel heterozygote mutation in the proband located at the third TGF-β-binding protein-like (TB) domain of the FBN1 g ene (NM000138: c.2066A>G: (p. Glu689Gly), NP_000129.3, in exon 17 of the gene). Co-segregation analysis with Sanger sequencing confirmed this mutation in the affected members of the pedigree. Conclusion: Our findings represent an autosomal dominant form of specific WMS resulting from a substitution mutation in the FBN1 g ene. In addition to the typical manifestations of the disorder, mild intellectual disability (ID) was identified in the 8-year-old proband. Given the fact that ID is primarily reported in ADAMTS10 mutated cases, this family was clinically and genetically a novel case.

citation_details.title: EEGDash Corpus: A Training-Ready Public Corpus for EEG Foundation Models
citation_details.author: Kuber Shahi, Bruno Aristimunha, Arnaud Delorme A
citation_details.abstract: Foundation models for electroencephalography (EEG) are pretrained on tens of thousands of hours of recordings, and their accuracy grows with that amount. Such data is hard to assemble. The largest sources are clinical archives that cannot be redistributed, and the public sources are spread over several archives, file formats, and licences. We release eegdash-corpus-v0, a training-ready corpus of 77 public EEG datasets, as the gated Hugging Face dataset EEGDash/eegdash-corpus-v0 with the SHA-256 of every file. REVE, the largest published EEG foundation model, names 89 datasets as its pretraining corpus. Twelve cannot be redistributed: four clinical archives that hold 82% of its hours, and eight under no-derivatives licences. The corpus holds the 76 others that REVE's sampling rate allows and one more from REVE's release card: 77 datasets, 14,075 hours from 7,272 subjects, 5.0 million 10-second samples and 6.21 billion tokens per epoch. Every dataset is fetched through EEGDash, converted once with REVE's recipe, and stored in its own buckets of a chunked Zarr store with its licence recorded beside it, so a model can train on the whole store or on any subset of datasets. To test that the store pretrains a model, we retrain REVE-Base from scratch twice with the authors' code, changed only in how it reads data, and score it on seven public OpenEEGBench tasks. It reaches 0.331 under linear probing and 0.273 after fine-tuning, against 0.333 and 0.325 for the released model and 0.200 and 0.205 for an untrained encoder. The converter, the conversion reports, and the loader changes are released with the corpus.
